parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify the substances liberated at the anode and at the cathode during the electrolysis of saturated $\text{KCl(aq)}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
When dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed, oxygen is liberated at the anode.

Dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed for $15.0$ minutes using a current of $0.750\text{ A}$.

Calculate the volume of oxygen that is liberated under room conditions.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The halogens chlorine, bromine and iodine differ in their strengths as oxidising agents. These strengths are indicated by the $E^\ominus$ values for these halogens.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Give the $E^\ominus$ values for chlorine, bromine and iodine acting as oxidising agents.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Deduce which of chlorine, bromine and iodine will react with a solution of $\text{Sn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ under standard conditions.

Explain your answer. Include a relevant equation in your explanation.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
An excess of chlorine is added to a solution of acidified $\text{Mn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ under standard conditions.

Give the formula of the product of this reaction that contains manganese.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: An electrochemical cell can be made by connecting an $\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}$ half-cell to an $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}/\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ half-cell under standard conditions.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the standard cell potential of this electrochemical cell.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: State the material that should be used as the electrode in each half-cell.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Describe **one** change to each half-cell that would **increase** the value of the cell potential. The temperature should remain at $298\text{ K}$.
